bovo-2025-put-that-there.previous_summary: This paper revisits multimodal window control in extended reality using a large language model. The system combines scene semantics, application state, speech, pointing and head orientation to determine window-placement actions. Users can issue direct instructions, refer to objects through speech and gestures, or express a broader task goal. The contribution is a context-sensitive interaction approach for organising an immersive workspace; it is not presented here as evidence of a measured productivity improvement.

colecchia-2025-immersive-healthcare-edit.previous_summary: This editorial introduces a collection on machine learning and immersive technologies in healthcare. It discusses interdisciplinary collaboration, ethical and stakeholder considerations, practical system development, medical education and wellbeing. The authors identify a need for human-centred and participatory design, inclusive evaluation and further clinical validation. This is an editorial synthesis of the collection, rather than an original empirical study.

jeon-2026-swapsense.previous_summary: SwapSense separates a reusable camera-based force sensor from interchangeable passive haptic components. A neural network estimates contact force from deformation images, while attached modules change how the interface feels. The evaluation examines generalisation across users and adaptation to previously unseen components. A perceptual study also characterises five haptic augmentations. The author record reports that adaptation used no more than a quarter of the target component’s data and less than 15 minutes of fine-tuning.

wang-2026-magicpen.previous_summary: MagicPen changes its length while remaining in contact with a physical surface, allowing a stylus to provide grounded feedback during VR modelling and drawing. A compliant mode follows geometry being edited, whereas a rigid mode constrains movement to an existing virtual surface. Three studies compare it with mid-air interaction in depth positioning and drawing tasks. The author record reports improved depth positioning and support for perceiving geometry through surface contact.

yi-2026-augmented-body-parts.previous_summary: This CHI workshop brings together research on virtual embodiment, wearable robotics, haptics and human augmentation. It examines how experience with unusual virtual bodies can inform the design and control of physical additions such as extra arms or tails. The programme combines a keynote, discussion of participants’ work and group activities to develop a shared research agenda. This record describes a workshop contribution, rather than an empirical evaluation of a robotic device.
